checkpoint_kv_scales.question: does dfranzen/intel-qwen3.8-flash-next-w4a16-autoround (the target cell 15 serves) carry calibrated k and v scales?
checkpoint_kv_scales.kaggle_copy: models/dfranzen/intel-qwen3.8-flash-next-w4a16-autoround/transformers/default/1: 50 files, no scale or kv file; config.json 266,426 B and quantization_config.json 94,026 B, the same sizes as the source below; model.safetensors.index.json is 513 B larger from Franzen's PLE reshard (ple_reshard_manifest.json). Kaggle model downloads ignore path= and stream the whole 181 GB archive, so the copy's own index was not read.
checkpoint_kv_scales.quantization: auto-round 0.15.0, int4 group 128 sym, packing auto_round:auto_gptq; no act_bits and no static_kv_dtype (static_kv_granularity 'tensor' is an AutoRound default key with nothing behind it)
checkpoint_kv_scales.full_attention_layer_tensors: q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj (BF16), q_norm, k_norm and the QSA indexer; nothing named k_scale, v_scale, kv_scale or output_scale
checkpoint_kv_scales.loader: SGLang's auto-round config gives quant methods only to linear and MoE layers (layers/quantization/auto_round.py get_quant_method), so attention never gets k_scale or v_scale parameters (radix_attention.py:127-128 leaves them None) whatever the checkpoint holds
checkpoint_kv_scales.consequence: every QSA layer's NVFP4 global scale stays 1.0 (fp4_kv_cache_quant_method.py:346 and 357), so a 16-value block's E4M3 scale is just its amax/6: full scale precision for blocks whose largest magnitude is 0.094 to 2,688, coarser subnormal scales below that, and no per-layer calibration. The FP8 cache runs uncalibrated at scale 1.0 today too. Lesilva measured +0.004 to +0.013 nats tail NLL in this same uncalibrated mode on another Flash-Next checkpoint; nvfp4kv_serve.parity measures our weights before any bench run.
checkpoint_kv_scales.recheck: python3 solution/sim/test_franzen_nvfp4kv.py --kv-scales (network: HF metadata files and the Kaggle file listing, about 24 MB)
